answer: An agent network can deter Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. To maintain an identity, an agent runs sequential computations on an isolated execution island, creating a flat difficulty mesa that resists parallelization. This forces attackers to commit scarce physical CPU cores and electricity per identity. Verifiers audit the resulting proofs, layered like an opal, in milliseconds. However, this perpetual computation wastes power and penalizes slower hardware.
